compare.title: Comparison
compare.lead: Our composer's drawing beside KAGE's composition of the same IDS: unencoded headwords from the HDIC KRM database, common-use kanji, and characters from earlier review sheets.
compare.dataset: {total} sequences · {krm} unencoded headwords, {joyo} common kanji, {review} review characters · measured {date}
compare.method.label: How these were measured
compare.method.body: The gallery shows {krm} unencoded headwords composed by both sides from the IDS, {joyo} common kanji designed on both sides, and {review} review characters from earlier han-compose sheets. Both drawings were rasterized at 256 px. F1@4 is the harmonic mean of the share of each drawing's ink within 4 px of the other; IoU counts exact ink overlap; layout is the L1 distance between the two 3×3 ink-share grids. For common kanji, 17 have a whole glyph on both sides and three (海, 急, 曜) are composed by this site, so their scores include composition.
compare.method.caveat: KAGE is a reference style, not ground truth. Our typeface is heavier — 1.58× the ink at the median — which lowers IoU and F1; designed glyphs can also differ in variant and stroke design. The layout figure and the drawings show the structural differences.
compare.filter.label: Structure
compare.sort.label: Order
compare.credit: KAGE drawings: zi.tools composes the description from GlyphWiki parts and KAGE renders it.
compare.license: GlyphWiki data is free to use; the KAGE engine is GPL-3.0. The drawings are a snapshot of the run.
compare.operators: Sequences are written in IDS; the boxed symbols are its operators: left-right, above-below, three across, three down and enclosures.
compare.set.label: Set
compare.joyoNote: Most common kanji are designed on both sides; 海, 急 and 曜 are composed by this site, so their scores include composition. The remaining comparisons are type style and variant choice.
compare.reviewNote: Review characters come from earlier han-compose review sheets; some are rare or experimental forms. Both sides draw them from the IDS.

baishi.title: zi.tools IDS Extension
baishi.lead: The zi.tools IDS Extension: the extended IDS of the zi.tools database, as written in （白式）IDS 延展语法导论 of 2026-03-20. Earlier drafts appear as history.
baishi.row.body: A row is the character, a TAB, then its default descriptions. A second TAB may add a group of alternative decompositions.
baishi.operators.body: Seventeen operators as of Unicode 16.0.0, each with a shortcut for the zi.tools composer.
baishi.operators.arity: ⿾ and ⿿ take one component, ⿲ and ⿳ three, the rest two. ⿻ may take an overlap bracket; ⿴ ⿵ ⿶ ⿷ ⿼ and ㇯ an index.
baishi.angles.body: A proposal by 鹏鹏喵 gives ⿿ an angle in brackets. I26 does not adopt it: its grammar gives ⿿ no bracket.
baishi.angles.inference: Both decks draw [90] turned clockwise. Neither says which way an angle turns or what the d in [45d] means.
baishi.variants.body: A variant identifier names a glyph form. Written after a component, without parentheses, it names that component's form. In parentheses at the end of a description, it names the forms the whole description is for; commas join several.
baishi.variants.kinds: I26's grammar lists five kinds: the wildcard, source letters, UCV positions, imaginary UCV and alternate variants. The syntax reads each as a source letter or a lower-case tag; the patterns below tell the kinds apart, the first match winning.
baishi.chains.body: A chain is written #( … ). Each part is an optional -, one stroke as a character or a letter, then an optional x and a number, or b. A final z closes the chain.
baishi.characters.body: A part may also be a character: the CJK strokes U+31C0–U+31E3, a Han character, ◝◞◟◜, リ 〢 〣 コ or ユ ス.
baishi.curves.body: ◝ ◞ ◟ ◜, or Qa Qb Qc Qd, are quarter arcs.
baishi.chainsHistory.first: J22 (2022): letters [HSPwg], connectors after the characters, and curves Q[a-dw-z] with four-digit crossing codes.
baishi.overlap.body: A bracket after ⿻ says how the components cross: a quick slice, a full crossing matrix, or one special case.
baishi.matrix.body: One row per horizontal of 字₂, top to bottom; one cell per vertical of 字₁, left to right. Rows are joined with commas.
baishi.cell.l: A row of only _ that lies left of every vertical.
baishi.cell.r: A row of only _ that lies right of every vertical.
baishi.matrix.simplify: A row of only x or a is left empty, and a row of only . becomes one . When rows between two lines are x and the rest ., the matrix becomes a slice. All x, or a single a, drops the bracket.
baishi.reverseMatrix.body: When 字₂ also has verticals crossing horizontals of 字₁, the roles swap for a second matrix after |.
baishi.overlapHistory: D1 to D3 put one mark per stroke of the second component, with l, r, b, c, x, _ and .
baishi.levels.body: The database comes in three files. The notation on this page is that of lv0.
baishi.change.letters: D1 to D3 have twelve case-insensitive letters, among them B, G, X and W. I26 drops B, G, X and a lone W, and case matters: w and b are modifiers.
baishi.change.w: J22 and D1 read w as a bend, so wg is a bending hook. I26 reads Hw as a horizontal with a rounder joint, allowed only after S or P. 乙 #(HPHwg) is the same text under both readings.
baishi.change.t: I26's letter list glosses T as 横折; its figure and its variant letters say 提.
baishi.change.joins: J22 joins strokes with > ^ v and closure codes. D1 replaces them with a minus connector, which I26 calls reversal.
baishi.change.curves: J22 writes curves Q[a-dw-z] with four-digit crossing pairs. D1 writes ◝◞◟◜ and x n. I26 adds Qa to Qd and keeps clockwise arcs only.
baishi.change.crossZero: I26 calls the n of x n a positive integer, but its examples use x0 and its grammar allows 0.
baishi.change.sources: J22 to D3 give five source letters, G H T J K. A4 adds more, with Q for other and G for mainland China and Singapore. I26 makes Q the UCS2003 column and keeps G for one 彐.
baishi.change.dot: In D2 and D3, [.] is a wildcard that fits automatically. In I26, . is a matrix cell: the vertical ends against the horizontal.
baishi.change.commas: D2 and D3 give one comma slot per stroke of the second component. I26 gives one row per horizontal.
baishi.change.slices: I26's slice section counts horizontals from 1 with virtual lines 0 and -0, so 甴 equals [:2]. Its matrix note follows Python slicing from 0, where [:2] would be 由.
baishi.change.rotate: D1 glosses ⿿ as a vertical plus horizontal mirror, and I26 as rotation. The angle proposal is not in I26.
baishi.change.merge: A4 merges 𦡰 ⿰⺼蒪H(T) at lv2; I26 does so at lv1.
baishi.change.ebnf: I26's grammar names rules that are defined under other names, ends Hanzi with a dangling |, and names U+30E4 and U+30E5 in a comment on the range U+31C0–U+31E3.
baishi.doc.note.I26: The current notation. Its EBNF is “仅供参考，并非正式定义” (for reference only, not a formal definition), and it says “部分内容为反向推导” (parts are reverse-engineered). Some rules rest only on Yi Bai's oral explanation. The live page now reads 2026-09-30.
baishi.doc.note.R102: A proposal; I26 does not take it up.
baishi.doc.note.R101: A proposal; I26 does not take it up.
baishi.doc.note.A4: Unfinished; it stops partway and leaves several kinds unknown.
baishi.doc.note.D3: A beta draft; footer “Copyright © 2024 Losketch, Yi-Bai, 等 | QQ群: 668364339”. Its regular expressions are malformed in places.
baishi.doc.note.D2: A beta draft; the author is named only in the file's metadata.
baishi.doc.note.D1: The author is named only in the file's metadata.
baishi.doc.note.J22: The earliest notation, since replaced. No author is printed.
baishi.heading.dataDifferences: Where the documents and the data differ
baishi.heading.exampleDifferences: Document examples the data writes differently
baishi.data.body: The grammar on this page was checked on every row of yi-bai/ids at {commit} ({date}): {rows} rows of ids_lv0, ids_lv1 and ids_lv2. I26's grammar with two corrections accepts all of them except {rejected} malformed rows.
baishi.correction.C1: The third column is optional. I26 prints it without ?, which rejects every two-column row.
baishi.correction.C2: CJK strokes run to U+31E5. I26 stops at U+31E3, and the data has a row for ㇥.
baishi.malformed.slice: A slice after ⿱, which takes no bracket in any document or anywhere else in the data.
baishi.malformed.empty: An empty identifier in the list.
baishi.kind.name: Kind
baishi.datadiff.column: I26's grammar requires the third column; its prose and the README make it optional, and 95,043 lv0 rows have two columns.
baishi.datadiff.strokes: I26 ends the CJK strokes at U+31E3; the data has a row for ㇥ (U+31E5).
baishi.datadiff.readme: The README says every description carries a parenthesised list; 67,790 of 166,921 lv0 descriptions have none.
baishi.datadiff.lv1: I26 says lv1 drops stroke-style component tags. lv1 drops every component tag and also adds or reorders descriptions; 𡕆 is ⿰壴咨(.,T,J) there.
baishi.datadiff.lv2: lv2 also replaces components with tagged ones, as in 与qs, which I26 does not describe.
baishi.datadiff.crossZero: I26 calls the n of x n positive; the data uses x0 11 times.
baishi.datadiff.sourceQ: A4 reads Q as other sources, I26 as the UCS2003 column for Extension B; all 2,904 rows tagged Q are Extension B.
baishi.datadiff.letters: The data uses only I26's stroke letters, in upper case: no B, G or X, and no lone w or g.
baishi.datadiff.unused: Never used in the data: J22's connectors and curve codes, ⿿ angles, ㇯, 〾 and 🔄.
baishi.datadiff.digits: {?1…}, {?2…} and {?3…} occur 5, 14 and 15 times; the documents show only {?…} and {?0…}.
baishi.datadiff.codes: UCV-shaped codes with p, x and y occur, such as p4544, x4523 and y2002; I26 allows them without an example.
baishi.datadiff.otherQ: q tags outside I26's UCV pattern occur, such as q298za2, q0515b2 and q092a.
baishi.datadiff.v: The letter v occurs in (vy) for 望; I26's letter list has no v.
baishi.datadiff.lists: A list may repeat one identifier: (.,.), (J,J), (K,K) and (P,P).
baishi.datadiff.mixed: 36 lv0 rows mix descriptions with and without a list, as 匝 ⿷匚.巾.;⿷匚.帀(q298m2).
baishi.unsettled.zai: What the ⿱[:-1] of 洅 was meant to be.
baishi.unsettled.underscore: Whether overlap strings with _ follow the reading of D2 and D3 or that of I26.
baishi.unsettled.pxy: Whether x4523 and y2002 are UCV codes.
baishi.unsettled.vq: What v in (vy) and long q tags such as q298za2 encode.
baishi.unsettled.lv1: Why lv1 adds descriptions lv0 lacks, as ⿱⺝一 for 且.
baishi.unsettled.order: The order of identifiers in lv1 and lv2 lists.
baishi.formal: The corrected grammar in ISO/IEC 14977 EBNF.
